title: POC commercial scoping & pilot guardrails - CloudWeave
header: Date: 2025-06-05T15:00Z | Duration: 58m | Recording: Fireflies export\nAttendees: Maya Chen, Samir Patel, Lena Ortiz (Redwood) / Ravi Menon, Aisha Karim, Daniel Park, Priya Rao (CloudWeave)
summary: High-level POC scoping to align success criteria, sizing, benchmark testcases, pilot credit allocation, and procurement runway. Customer wants 4-week functional POC + 2-week perf/baseline benchmarking. Key commercial ask: clarity on credits, overage policy, and path to a reserved contract if POC hits SLOs.
topics: POC success criteria and acceptance tests
Workload sizing and test data volumes
Pilot economic guardrails: credits, timeboxed terms, overage handling
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Real quick intros?
[00:12] Ravi Menon: Hi I'm Ravi, Head of ML at CloudWeave. We're evaluating inference platforms for our summarization and rerank pipelines.
[00:20] Samir Patel: Samir, I'm the solutions engineer from Redwood, I'll run through perf expectations and run some tail-latency thoughts.
[00:28] Aisha Karim: Aisha here, CTO, I'll be watching procurement and security knobs.
[00:34] Maya Chen: Awesome. Goal for today is to align on success criteria for the POC, how much commit/credits we expect to offer, and what bench tests we'll run.
[01:05] Ravi Menon: High level — we want a functional proof that your hosted API can meet our p95 latency target of ~250ms and that cost-per-1k tokens beats our current infra. Also need to validate private deployment later but this POC is on hosted to move faster.
[01:30] Samir Patel: Cool. Two tracks: functional correctness/quality — e.g. summarization ROUGE-ish tests and human evals — and performance: throughput with concurrent inferences, p50/p95/p99, and cold vs warm KV cache behavior.
[01:47] Priya Rao: Question: when you say KV cache behavior, we're concerned how long the prefix cache takes to warm up and how that impacts cost math.
[01:55] Samir Patel: Yep, we'll instrument that. For the POC we'll do a staged run: synthetic warmup of chat-style prefixes then steady-state tests. We can capture token-level billing too.
[02:15] Daniel Park: From procurement, the pilot needs a clear credit envelope and explicit overage policy. We don't want surprise charges.
[02:24] Lena Ortiz: Understood. Our recommended guarded pilot is a 6-week engagement with a fixed credit pool. Typically we allocate credits that map to expected token consumption for the agreed benchmark runs plus a buffer.
[02:40] Aisha Karim: What's the typical buffer?
[02:43] Maya Chen: Usually 20-30% depending on uncertainty. For you, given multiple endpoints and reranking bursts, I'd suggest 30% buffer.
[02:52] Ravi Menon: We need to make sure the benchmarks are realistic. Our reranker receives 16 candidates, does a batch rerank, and generates a short justification. This is more compute-heavy per query.
[03:08] Samir Patel: We'll size based on tokens-per-query and average inference length. Can you share a sample payload distribution? If not, we'll use a conservative estimate and tune once you share telem.
[03:24] Ravi Menon: We can share anonymized distributions — I'll send a CSV.
[03:28] Maya Chen: Great. For acceptance criteria let's propose: (1) p95 latency <= 250ms for 1 RPS steady-state for summarize endpoint, (2) rerank throughput > 20 qps with p95 < 400ms for batched rerank, (3) quality delta within 5% vs baseline on standardized eval set, (4) billing within allocated credits. Does that sound reasonable?
[04:05] Aisha Karim: The quality delta metric — are you describing automated metrics only or will there be a human eval holdout?
[04:12] Samir Patel: Both. We'll run automated metrics (BLEU/ROUGE/precision@k for rerank) and a small human eval (n=200 samples) to validate.
[04:21] Ravi Menon: Sounds ok. Timeline?
[04:25] Lena Ortiz: We're thinking 4-week execution window: week 0 onboarding and integration, week 1 functional tests & quality, week 2 performance tuning and benchmarks, week 3 final tests + write-up. Plus 2 weeks buffer for procurement/ops. So 6 weeks total as mentioned.
[04:44] Daniel Park: For procurement we need an SOW with milestone-based acceptance: sign-off after final test report and a pathway to convert credits to committed reserved capacity within 30 days of sign-off.
[04:58] Maya Chen: We can do that. Our standard pilot MSA has language about credits expiring at the end of the pilot but we can include a conversion credit clause if you go to reserve.
[05:12] Priya Rao: Security questions — SOC2, data residency, encryption at rest keys. If we go to private there are extra items — but for this hosted pilot we need an NDA and SOC2 report.
[05:26] Maya Chen: We'll share SOC2 Type II and our security whitepaper. We can also redact logs as part of the pilot if needed.
[05:34] Ravi Menon: Overage policy detail? If we exceed credits because tests ran longer due to bug, what happens?
[05:40] Lena Ortiz: For pilots we set a hard cap unless you explicitly authorize overage. If a test needs extra run we request a one-off credit top-up and document it.
[05:49] Daniel Park: That's acceptable. We also need invoice terms and exportable billing CSVs for audit.
[05:56] Maya Chen: We provide token-level billing CSVs and can supply per-route breakdowns.
[06:04] Samir Patel: Operational notes: we'll instrument per-request traces and provide the benchmark harness as a script you can run from your infra. We'll also include a reproducible dataset and test config.
[06:18] Ravi Menon: Who's the execution owner for Redwood?
[06:21] Maya Chen: I'll own the commercial, Lena will manage credits and invoicing, and Samir will run the benchmark tests with you.
[06:29] Priya Rao: Internal ramp: we need a small on-call window because tests may spike infra.
[06:35] Samir Patel: We'll coordinate a narrow maintenance window and provide runbooks.
[06:40] Maya Chen: Let's go into specific numbers. Based on our quick calc, if your average token per summarize request is 600 tokens and you plan 1,500 sample requests for quality + 10k benchmark inferences, that's roughly X tokens — we estimate the pilot to consume ~1.2M tokens, plus rerank runs might add another 400k tokens. With 30% buffer that's ~2.1M tokens.
[07:10] Ravi Menon: Ok ballpark is fine. What's that convert to credits?
[07:14] Lena Ortiz: Our standard conversion for hosted pilot credits: 1 credit = 1,000 tokens for the simple metric in the sheet we'll send. So 2.1M tokens ~ 2100 credits. We'll propose a 2500 credit pilot.
[07:28] Daniel Park: And price per credit?
[07:30] Maya Chen: We'll share a pilot pricing sheet. Pilots are often priced at a promotional rate to de-risk evaluation. If you convert to Dedicated, we'll roll pilot usage as a discount toward committed spend if within 30 days.
[07:45] Aisha Karim: We need a clear runway to procurement — typical cycle is 6-8 weeks after sign-off.
[07:51] Daniel Park: Correct. Our timeline: review pilot SOW this week, sign pilot within 7 business days, run pilot 6 weeks, internal procurement review matches up to 8 weeks for a reserved contract.
[08:05] Priya Rao: For the benchmark harness, please make it cloud-agnostic. We will run it from our GCP environment and need a downloadable docker image.
[08:15] Samir Patel: We'll provide a dockerized harness and scripts to replay your payload distributions, including flags for batch sizing and concurrency.
[08:22] Ravi Menon: For success criteria, I want an explicit test that simulates our 16-candidate rerank in a single batched call — that tends to be the heaviest.
[08:31] Samir Patel: Agreed. We'll include a 'rerank_16' scenario in the benchmark matrix.
[08:36] Maya Chen: On next steps, Redwood will: share pilot SOW, share security docs, ship pilot pricing and credit mapping sheet, and deliver benchmark harness. CloudWeave will share anonymized payload distribution and confirm sign-off owners.
[08:52] Daniel Park: Action: I'll circulate procurement checklist and required PO template.
[09:00] Aisha Karim: One more — how do you handle model fallbacks if capacity constrained? We need graceful degradation tests.
[09:08] Samir Patel: We have routing policies and model-variant fallbacks. For the pilot we'll enable a lower-cost fallback with explicit acceptance tests that checks semantic divergence within your threshold.
[09:20] Ravi Menon: Great. Anything else?
[09:23] Maya Chen: Let's document timeline: draft SOW by 2025-06-09, pilot sign-off target 2025-06-16, onboarding week start 2025-06-23, final report by 2025-08-04. Does that align?
[09:39] Daniel Park: Yes.
[09:41] Lena Ortiz: I'll include milestone payment/credit draws in the SOW so your finance can see cashflow.
[09:48] Priya Rao: Please also include a pre-approved change request process so extra test runs can be signed quickly.
[09:55] Maya Chen: Will do. Thanks everyone.
[10:00] [meeting closed]

Note: Transcript contains occasional mis-hearings e.g., "KV cash" for KV cache, and speaker labels may shift in a few segments.
